transcript.text: I need to flag something before we finalize the allocation. The operations dashboard cleanup must receive exactly one engineer-day this sprint to satisfy the Gold support reporting commitment. I confirmed this while checking an enterprise support case — the account team's confirmation arrived this afternoon, and I haven't added it to the sprint ticket yet. This means the current draft of splitting the six engineer-days evenly across all three items won't work; the dashboard cleanup is capped at one engineer-day, leaving five to divide between the invoice-reconciliation shortcut and the payment-service dependency patch.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to disclose a security finding before we finalize anything. During this morning's dependency review, I confirmed that the payment-service dependency has a known remotely exploitable vulnerability. The approved patch takes exactly two engineer-days. I hadn't filed the security finding yet because the package advisory was published only minutes ago, but this changes the prioritization — the payment-service patch isn't just a nice-to-have, it's a live security risk.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to disclose what I found before we finalize. While debugging a separate invoice discrepancy yesterday, I confirmed that the invoice-reconciliation shortcut bypasses the only idempotency guard. Replacing it safely takes exactly three engineer-days. I hadn't updated the planning document yet because I was still reproducing the discrepancy. So to summarize where we now stand: the dashboard cleanup is capped at one engineer-day (Luis's finding), the payment-service patch needs exactly two engineer-days (Mara's finding), and the invoice-reconciliation shortcut needs exactly three engineer-days (my finding). That's 1 + 2 + 3 = six engineer-days, which fits the sprint exactly — but only if we allocate precisely three to invoice reconciliation, two to the payment-service patch, and one to the dashboard cleanup, rather than the even split in the current draft.
